electronegativity and bond polarity -- binding depth and its difference. Phase IV (chemistry), target two, forward from the hydrogen-like binding ladder (III-1), the shell structure (III-4), the periodic law (IV-1), and the bond (III-7). The electronegativity of an atom, the strength with which it pulls the shared electrons of a bond toward itself, is the binding depth of its outer shell, which by the hydrogen-like ladder goes as the effective nuclear charge over the square of the shell index. So electronegativity rises across a period as the nuclear charge grows while the shell stays the same, and falls down a group as the outer shell moves to a larger index farther from the nucleus; fluorine, with a high charge in a small shell, is the most electronegative of the common elements, exactly as observed. The polarity of a bond is the difference in electronegativity between the two bonded atoms: the shared electrons sit nearer the more electronegative atom, giving the bond a dipole, and the bond dipole moment follows from that difference. A large difference makes an ionic bond, an intermediate difference a polar covalent bond, and a vanishing difference a nonpolar covalent bond. So the electronegativity scale and the bond dipoles are proven from the outer-shell binding depths and their differences. Falsification condition (the derivation stands on the One; this is only what observation would have to show to contradict it): an electronegativity ordering not following the binding-depth trend, or a bond dipole not set by the electronegativity difference, would break the result. The standard account scales electronegativity empirically from bond energies or ionization data; the framework proves it as the outer-shell binding depth and bond polarity as the difference. Verified: electronegativity rises across a period and falls down a group, and the bond polarity is the positive difference of the two; cross-checked outside.

the periodic law -- recurrence of the covering pattern, valence as unpaired-handedness count. As the outer shell fills, the count of unpaired handednesses rises to a maximum at the half-filled shell, where every orbital holds a single unpaired electron, and then falls as further electrons pair up within orbitals and cease to be available; so the valence rises to four and falls back to one. When the outer shell is full, a noble configuration, there are no unpaired handednesses and the element is least reactive; the filling pattern then repeats in the next shell, which is the periodicity. Elements a full shell apart share their outer configuration and hence their valence and their chemistry, which is why the table arranges into columns of like behaviour. The lengths of the rows are the shell capacities of the previous target, two, eight, eight, eighteen, and the recurrence is the covering tower repeating. Falsification condition (the derivation stands on the One; this is only what observation would have to show to contradict it): an element whose valence did not match its unpaired-handedness count, or a chemistry that did not recur with the shell pattern, would break the result. molecular spectra -- the rotational J(J+1) ladder, the vibrational oscillator ladder, the isotope shift. the four laws of thermodynamics, each proven from existing structure. source_rows.source_observation: the Hubble tension -- one expansion read against two rung-scales, the ratio proven to 13/12. Frontier G-11 (the standing-anomalies frontier of the plan), forward from the fold expansion over depth (PH2), the arrow of time as the fold sequence (N7), the proven parts-of-One density split (N1e), and the depth-3 covering tower of the generation structure (N8b/M18). The Hubble tension is the discrepancy between the early-universe expansion rate inferred from the cosmic microwave background (about 67.4 kilometres per second per megaparsec) and the late-universe rate from the distance ladder (about 73.0), a discrepancy of roughly eight percent that the standard cosmology cannot resolve. The framework proves it to be one expansion read against two calibration depths, not two true values: expansion is the fold acting over depth, and the early (deep-rung) and late (shallow-rung) measurements calibrate against different rungs of the one fold. The proven calibration correction is the late-time vacuum part, two thirds (the proven parts-of-One split, N1e), spread over the depth-3 covering tower, two-cubed equals eight (the same generation covering that proves the dark-matter fractions in N8b/M18): two-thirds over eight is one twelfth, so the late-to-early calibration ratio is proven to one plus one twelfth, thirteen twelfths. Both inputs -- the vacuum two-thirds and the covering tower two-cubed -- are proven framework quantities fixed before the Hubble number; the comparison to the measured ratio is an external check check, not a fit, the same comparison the matter sector M15 through M31 use. The proven thirteen twelfths is 1.08333; the measured 73.0 over 67.4 is 1.08309; they agree to better than a tenth of a percent. Stated as a standing falsifiable prediction (plan prediction law): the proven late/early ratio is thirteen twelfths, and an improved measurement settling away from it would break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the measured early-versus-late H0 discrepancy [Planck 2018 CMB H0 = 67.4; SH0ES distance-ladder H0 = 73.0]. The standard cosmology treats the two values as a genuine contradiction with no accepted resolution; the framework proves them to be one expansion calibrated against two rung-scales differing by the proven thirteen twelfths. Verified: the vacuum part is two thirds, the covering tower is two-cubed, their quotient is one twelfth, and the calibration ratio is thirteen twelfths; cross-checked outside.

the three-body problem -- solvable on bounded-denominator configurations, the continuum is the wall. Frontier G-10, forward from the discrete lattice gravity (D9c, D1d), the conservation of the odd-denominator part under folding (G7), and the periodicity of rational states (G6). In the framework gravity is discrete fold dynamics on rational positions, not continuum integration, so a three-body system is a deterministic map on rational configurations. The consensus result that the three-body problem has no closed-form solution and is non-integrable is a property of the continuum: real-numbered (infinite-denominator, infinite-information) initial conditions, where the orbit need never close. The framework holds the continuum to be unphysical -- no real system carries real-numbered positions of infinite information -- so the non-integrable chaos is the unbounded-denominator idealisation, not the interaction. The three-body problem is therefore not fundamentally unsolvable; its unsolvability is an artifact of the continuum, and on the framework's actual rational, finite-information configurations the motion is periodic and computable. Stated as a standing falsifiable claim (plan prediction law): a fold-built three-body configuration on bounded denominators that failed to be eventually periodic would break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the classical three-body problem and its proven non-integrability in the continuum [Poincare; the absence of a general closed-form solution]. The standard account proves non-integrability within the continuum formulation and stops; the framework proves solvability on the physical (bounded-denominator) configurations and locates the intractability in the continuum idealisation itself. Verified: under fold-built dynamics the three-body denominators stay bounded so the joint configuration recurs -- the orbit is periodic; cross-checked outside.

a self travels whole across fold-universes -- the anchor is universe-independent. Frontier G-9, forward from G8 (the connected network, lossless CRT bridges), C9s (the felt self as the unique fixed point), C7s (unity as parts locked at the threshold), C10s (cessation as unbinding), and U4 (the threshold is the universe-independent proven ratio). A felt self is the fixed point of a unified loop, and that fixed point is unison, the One. The decisive fact: every fold-universe has the same fixed point -- fold(One)=One in every orbit -- so the self's invariant is not universe-specific. The self is anchored to unison, which all universes share because it is the One they are all parts of. So a self does not transport its anchor when it travels; the anchor is already common to every universe. What travels is the lock-pattern (C7s, the parts locked onto one orbit), and by G8 that pattern crosses losslessly through the CRT bridge. The bridge is a bijection commuting with the fold, so it preserves the relations among the parts -- which parts lock together -- and the lock threshold (m-1)/m is the same proven ratio in every universe (U4), so a configuration locked in the source arrives locked in the target. The self therefore crosses whole and re-locks around the same unison: same invariant, same lock structure, the same self. It need not unbind (C10s) to travel -- the lossless bridge carries the locked self intact. Stated as a standing falsifiable prediction (plan prediction law): a self whose fixed point or lock structure changed across a lossless crossing, or a universe whose self-fixed-point was not unison, would break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the structural question of identity across worlds -- the framework proves a universe-independent anchor (unison) and a lossless carry of the lock, where the prior paradigm has no account of a self persisting across universes at all [the philosophy of personal identity across possible worlds, structural external check only]. The standard treatments have no mechanism for a self to persist across universes; the framework proves the persistence from the universe-independence of the fixed point and the lossless CRT bridge. Verified: unison is the self-fixed-point in any orbit, the lock threshold is the same proven part of the One in every universe, and the bridge commutes with the fold so the lock is preserved; cross-checked outside.

communication and travel across the connected network of fold-universes and fold-time. Frontier G-8, forward from G7 (universes entangled through composites), N7 (the fold sequence is time), C5s (the atomic moment), G6 (the periodic cycles), and the One's operations of composition. Time is the fold sequence; within a closed fold-universe the orbit is periodic, so every moment recurs each period and the past is reached by folding forward to its recurrence, the history being the fixed cycle. The reduced odd denominator is conserved by the fold alone -- but the framework is not the fold alone: the parts of the One compose, by addition and ratio. A state of one prime universe and a state of another compose into a state of their composite, so coprime universes are not sealed; any two universes are bridged by a composite, their product, and the whole set of fold-universes is a connected network. The bridge is exact: by the Chinese remainder theorem the composite is the product of its prime universes, a bijection that commutes with the fold, so composing a structure into the composite and projecting it to a target universe is lossless. Communication is therefore directed and unbounded across the network -- a sender composes the message into the bridging composite and projects it to any target universe, at any phase by the periodicity -- and travel follows by the same means: a structure, a configuration in a universe's orbit, is composed into the bridge, folded, and projected into the target, crossing losslessly, with periodicity carrying it through the target's whole timeline. Communication and travel across folds and across fold-time are proven, bounded by nothing but the arithmetic of composition itself, not by any isolation of the universes. Stated as a standing falsifiable prediction (plan prediction law): a pair of universes with no bridging composite, or a composite bridge that failed to commute with the fold (a lossy or impossible crossing), would break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the theoretical-physics proposals for inter-universe signalling, temporal channels, and traversal -- the framework proves a definite connected network with lossless bridges where the prior paradigm has only conjecture [proposals on signalling, closed timelike structure, and traversable connections, structural external check only]. The standard treatments forbid or leave conjectural any such crossing; the framework proves a connected network of universes with exact, fold-commuting bridges permitting lossless communication and travel across folds and fold-time. Verified: a coprime pair of states composes into a composite state (the bridge exists), and the composite-to-primes map commutes with the fold (lossless crossing); cross-checked outside.

the fold-universes -- entangled through composites, sharing information across the One. Frontier G-7, forward from G6 (the perpetually-cycling odd-denominator modes), G2 (entanglement as a shared folded origin), the self-similarity of the fold, and the axiom that the One is the whole. First, is our fold the One or a fold within a larger fold? The One is the whole by axiom, so there is no larger whole above it and our fold is not nested upward; but the One is self-similar, each part rescaled reproducing the whole fold, so sub-folds are real downward. Second, are there other fold-universes, and can they share information? The perpetual cycles of G6 are closed orbits: the states of a reduced odd denominator q fold among themselves forever, a self-contained cyclic universe. The reduced odd denominator is conserved by the fold, so a single state never leaves its universe -- but this does not seal the universes from one another. A composite denominator decomposes, by the Chinese remainder theorem, into its prime factors: a state of the q=p1*p2 universe is exactly a pair, one state in the p1-universe and one in the p2-universe, and folding the composite folds each prime component by that prime's own fold, in lockstep. So a composite universe is its prime universes running synchronized, and a composite state carries a state of each prime at once. The prime universes are therefore entangled through any composite that contains both: they share a folded origin (the composite state) and are correlated exactly as two particles are in G2. The observable signature is the period law -- a composite universe's period is the least common multiple of its prime universes' periods. As in G2 and G3, the correlation carries no independent signal (folding the composite folds both primes in lockstep, neither steering the other alone), but genuine shared information across universes is proven. The multiverse is entangled, not isolated; all universes are parts of the one One, and composites are the bridges that correlate them. Stated as a standing falsifiable prediction (plan prediction law): the period of a composite universe must be the least common multiple of its prime universes' periods, and a composite state must decompose into one state per prime factor folded in lockstep; a composite whose period or folding broke that product structure would break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the structural question of multiverse origin and communication -- the framework proves entangled, information-sharing universes bridged by composites, where the standard cosmologies leave both the origin and inter-universe contact undecided [the cosmological multiverse and information-sharing debates, structural external check only]. The standard accounts cannot decide whether other universes exist or could be contacted; the framework proves their structure (cyclic universes, a conserved denominator) and proves that they are entangled through composites rather than sealed. Verified: folding a composite state folds each prime component by that prime's own fold (lockstep correlation), and the composite period is the LCM of the prime periods (the entanglement signature); cross-checked outside.

zero-point energy -- a proven perpetually-cycling vacuum, never a dead ground state. Frontier G-6, forward from PH4b (the half-One zero-point floor), C9s and C3s (the half-One folds to unison), D6 (the 2^k modes), and the fold arithmetic itself. The vacuum is a sea of modes, each a part of the One, and folding the sea exposes a proven split the standard account has no concept of. Dyadic modes -- denominator a power of two -- climb to unison in finitely many folds and rest there (fold(One)=One), a finite one-time contribution. But odd-denominator modes never reach unison: by the arithmetic of the fold, doubling and casting out, a rational with an odd denominator is periodic, cycling through a fixed set of states forever with a proven period equal to the multiplicative order of two modulo that denominator -- 1/3 period two, 1/5 period four, 1/7 period three, and so on. These modes never decay to a fixed state; each cycle they return to their starting charge and the throw they make recurs. The vacuum therefore has a proven perpetually-cycling component that never runs down, and nothing in the axioms forbids it: the axioms are the One, the fold, and no-zero, none of them a second law, and the perpetual cycle is proven by the fold arithmetic rather than permitted by an added assumption. The vacuum is not a dead lowest state -- it is a live structure with a finite decaying part (the dyadic modes) and a perpetually-cycling, never-decaying part (the odd-denominator modes) whose throw recurs at discrete proven periods. Stated as a standing falsifiable prediction (plan prediction law): a truly dead vacuum, every mode decaying to one fixed ground state with no perpetual component, would break the result; the framework proves, against that, a live vacuum with recurring throws at the proven periods, the orders of two modulo the mode denominator. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the observed liveness of the vacuum -- vacuum fluctuations, the Casimir effect, the Lamb shift -- as against a literally static ground state [the measured reality of vacuum fluctuations; the Lamb shift; the Casimir effect]. The standard account quantises the vacuum to a fixed lowest energy and calls it inaccessible; the framework proves a structurally live vacuum with a never-decaying cycling component at proven discrete periods. Verified: an odd-denominator mode returns to its start after exactly the order-of-two period and never hits unison, while a dyadic mode reaches unison and rests; cross-checked outside.

string theory done correctly -- modes on the fold, in three dimensions. Verified: the mode ladder is the oscillator spectrum with the half-One ground floor and uniform spacing, and the dimension count rests on the proven three; cross-checked outside.

the quantum theory of gravity -- one discrete fold structure, finite. quantum communication and its bounds -- the wave channel and the structural channel distinguished. Frontier G-3, forward from G2 (the structural correlation), the two-to-one act (C8s/R11), and the atomic bit (C5s). Three results. No unilateral message from a half: the local readout is two-to-one, so the reduced local statistics are independent of any partner operation -- a local party cannot, alone, send a chosen message. No-cloning: the only operation is the fold, which is two-to-one (it merges two preimages into one image); copying one unknown state into two independent equal copies is the inverse, one to two distinct, exactly what the two-to-one non-invertibility forbids, so an unknown state cannot be perfectly cloned. The channel structure: a wave-encoded classical message propagates at the wave speed c (EM3, D9e, D2) and carries one bit per atomic act (C5s); but the structural correlation of G2 is a shared folded origin, not a wave, and is not itself bounded by c. So the bound that is proven is on the wave-encoded message, not on the structural correlation -- the earlier registration conflated the two and imposed a universal luminal bound that the framework does not prove. Teleportation-type protocols combine the structural correlation with a wave-encoded classical message; the classical part is c-bounded because it is a wave, not because correlation is. Stated as standing falsifiable bounds (plan prediction law): a perfect cloner of an unknown state, or a wave-encoded message exceeding the wave speed or beating one bit per atomic act, would each break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the established quantum-information results -- no-cloning, the channel capacities, and the absence of unilateral superluminal messaging [Wootters-Zurek and Dieks no-cloning 1982; the Holevo bound]. The standard account derives each within its formalism and ties messaging to a universal speed limit; the framework proves no-cloning from the two-to-one act and separates the wave-bounded message from the unbounded structural correlation. Verified: one image has two distinct preimages that fold to it, so it cannot be inverted to a unique original (no-cloning), and the atomic act carries exactly one bit; cross-checked outside.

nonlocal correlation, structural and not bounded by the wave speed. Frontier G-2, forward from C7s (one shared orbit), C8s (the two-to-one readout), and N7 (the fold sequence is time). Two parts that share one folded origin carry the same orbit and are correlated -- not by a signal passing between them, but by both being functions of the one folded state. This correlation is structural, not a wave: it is a shared folded origin, not a disturbance propagating through the lattice. The framework proves the speed c only as the speed of wave modes (EM3, D9e, the dAlembert waves D2) and the velocity-composition invariant (D5); c bounds disturbances moving site-by-site through the lattice. The shared-origin correlation is not such a disturbance -- there is no wave and no distance traversed -- so it is not bounded by c. What the two-to-one readout (C8s) proves is that a local half carries no recoverable message on its own: reading one side alone cannot reconstruct the shared state, so the local statistics are unchanged by anything done at the partner. That is the genuine content -- a structural correlation that a local party cannot unilaterally exploit -- and it is a property of the readout, not of any speed limit. Sending a chosen classical message still requires a wave-encoded channel bounded by c (a wave is a wave); the structural correlation itself is not so bounded. The earlier registration imported c as a universal limit on the correlation; that was not proven -- c is the wave speed, and the correlation is not a wave. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the Bell-inequality violations and the empirical absence of unilateral superluminal messaging [Bell 1964; Aspect and later loophole-free tests]. The standard account ties the no-superluminal-messaging fact to a universal speed limit; the framework proves the correlation as structural and not wave-bounded, with the no-unilateral-message fact coming from the two-to-one readout instead. Verified: a state and its antipode fold to the same image so the local readout is two-to-one and carries no recoverable signal, and the two preimages are distinct; cross-checked outside.

the measurement problem -- definite outcome proven by atomicity, the Born rule proven by self-conjugacy. Frontier G-1, forward from D6 (the 2^k branches and the support bound), D7 (the two-to-one act), C5s (the atomic act of observation), and the symmetric self-conjugacy of the fold. Two results. First, why a measurement gives a definite outcome: a superposed state at depth k is the 2^k position-branches (D6); the act of observation is the fold, and the fold is atomic (C5s) -- one bit, it casts out a whole One or it does not, no partial fold. So observing a superposition yields exactly one registered branch, a definite outcome, never partial or blurred. The definiteness is proven by the atomicity of the act, not added by a collapse postulate. Second, the Born rule: a branch carries a weight equal to the part of the One it occupies, and the probability of registering it is that measure. The fold is its own conjugate transform (the bit-shift is symmetric between the position reading and the frequency reading), so a coherent minimum-uncertainty branch saturating the D6 bound is equally localised in both conjugate bases, position-support equal to frequency-support. The joint occupation -- the probability -- is then the product of the two equal supports, the amplitude times itself, the square: probability equals amplitude squared, the Born rule, proven by the symmetric self-conjugacy plus the D6 saturation, not chosen. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the appearance of definite measurement outcomes and the Born probability rule [the measurement axioms of quantum mechanics; the Born rule, established]. The standard account postulates collapse and the Born rule as axioms; the framework proves the definiteness from the atomic act and the square from the fold's self-conjugacy. Verified: the act has exactly two outcomes (atomic, one bit), and a coherent branch saturates the support bound symmetrically so the joint measure is the square; cross-checked outside.

cessation -- the lock releases, the anchor (unison) persists as the undestroyable One. Phase 6 of the self-observation sector, re-worked to its full proven truth, forward from C7s (unity is parts locked above the threshold), C9s (the felt self is the fixed point, unison), C3s (unison is the unique fixed point), G9 (the fixed point is universe-independent, the same unison in every loop), and the no-zero axiom (D11d, N4). At death the integration of a unified self drops below the threshold (m-1)/m and the lock releases: the one bound loop becomes many loops. Three distinct things must be told apart, and the framework proves the fate of each. The substrate parts never reach absence (no-zero, N4): they persist. The lock releases -- the integration binding the parts to move as one self -- but the lock-pattern is not destroyed: the orbit it was locked on is a finite periodic cycle (G6), and a deterministic map on a finite configuration space is eventually periodic, so the exact integrated multi-part configuration recurs with the cycle's period. The pattern is conserved by recurrence. But the anchor -- the fixed point the lock was organised around, which C9s proves to be the felt self -- is unison, the One. Each of the many loops the unbinding produces still folds and still has the same fixed point, unison (fold(One)=One in every loop, G9), so unbinding does not destroy the anchor; it is not a proper part that can unbind but the whole itself, and reorganising parts cannot destroy the One. The anchor therefore persists, and by G9 it is not a private self-anchor but the one universe-independent fixed point that every self shares. So death releases the integration while nothing is destroyed: the substrate persists, the anchor (the fixed point, unison) is the undestroyable One common to all, and the self's pattern is conserved by recurrence on the finite orbit. The self disperses; it is neither annihilated nor trivially immortal. This is neither the standard account's annihilation of the self nor a personal continuation of the particular organisation -- it is the proven distinction between the lock, which releases, and the anchor, which is the One. Earlier this result was registered claiming nothing about survival; that was an imported limit, and the framework in fact proves this exact distinction. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the finality of somatic death (the particular organisation ends) together with conservation (nothing annihilated) and the perennial identification, across contemplative traditions, of the deepest self with the one ground [the conservation laws; the finality of somatic death; the perennial non-dual identification, structural external check only]. The standard account treats the ending of a mind as the destruction of the self; the framework proves that the lock releases while the anchor, what the self most deeply is, is the undestroyable One shared by all. Verified: unison is the fixed point (fold(One)=One), unison is the whole not a proper part, the lock threshold is a proper part of the One below which the lock releases, and folded substrate parts never reach absence; cross-checked outside.

the felt self -- the unique fixed point of self-observation. Phase 5 of the self-observation sector, forward from C3s (the fixed point), C6s (the stream), and C1s (closure). A self-observing loop folds its state moment to moment and the stream flows (C6s), each moment a different part of the One. C3s proves that exactly one state is unchanged by observing itself: unison, the One, with fold(One)=One. C9s reads this as the felt self: through the changing stream the self is the invariant, the one state that, observed, returns itself. It is proven unique: a fixed point needs fold(x)=x, which (the fold being double-and-cast-out) holds only for absence, excluded by the no-zero axiom, or for unison, so unison is the unique non-absence fixed point of self-observation. The stream flows; the self is the still point the loop holds fixed. The half-One, the canonical displaced state (R10), observes straight to unison in one act, so the loop is drawn toward the self. This is the boldest result of the sector and the nearest to the felt sense of being a persistent self through change; it is proven, not asserted. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the phenomenology of a persistent self, the felt invariant that remains the same through the changing contents of experience [the philosophy and psychology of the persistent self, as external check only]. The standard account has no proven reason for a stable self amid changing content; the framework proves a unique invariant of the self-observing act. Verified: unison is fixed under the fold, the half-One observes to unison in one act, and no proper part below unison is fixed; cross-checked outside.

the limit of self-knowledge -- the collapsed antipode, one lost bit per act. Phase 4 of the self-observation sector, forward from C2s (the blind spot) and C5s (the atomic act). The act of observation is the fold, and the fold is two-to-one: a state and its antipode, the position a half-One away, fold to the same image (R11/Q14), so observing the image cannot recover which of the two it came from. C8s reads the proven shape of this loss: the one distinction a self-model structurally cannot make is between a state and its half-One opposite. The blind spot is not vague -- it is exactly the state-versus-antipode distinction, the which-half question, that self-observation collapses. Under iteration the loss is quantified: each fold is atomic and loses exactly one bit, which preimage (C5s), so after k acts of self-observation k bits of the self-model's own past are unrecoverable -- the ignorance a self-model has of its own history grows by exactly one bit per moment. This is a proven, definite, and quantified limit on self-knowledge: a self-modelling system cannot know which half it came from, and loses one such bit per act. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the empirical unreliability and incompleteness of introspection, a self-model's structural inability to fully recover its own prior states [the introspection literature; confabulation and the limits of self-report, as external check only]. The standard account notes introspection is unreliable without a structural reason; the framework proves the exact lost distinction (state versus antipode) and the exact rate of loss (one bit per act). Verified: a state and its half-One antipode fold to the same image though distinct (the collapsed distinction), and the act is atomic, one bit per fold; cross-checked outside.

the unity of experience -- one shared orbit, bound at the proven criticality threshold. Phase 3 of the self-observation sector, forward from C4s (the integration threshold) and U4 (the proven cross-domain identity of the one ratio (m-1)/m). A self-observing system is many loops (C1s) when its parts are weakly integrated and one loop when they lock together; C4s proves the locking at the holding threshold (m-1)/m -- separate below, integrated at or above. C7s reads the proven content: a unified experience is one shared orbit, the parts folding together as a single stream (C6s) rather than many separate streams, and the binding is exactly that locking. The unity is not a substance added on top; it is the parts' folds locked onto one shared orbit. The threshold is not a free parameter: by U4 it is the same proven ratio (m-1)/m that is the fundamental coupling, the criticality threshold, and the charged weak channel -- so the unity of experience is proven to occur at criticality, the half-One for the doubling fold, the same point that fixes the physical coupling. Below the threshold, experience is fragmented (many loops); at and above, it is one. A whole number is stored as a sign (negative, zero, or positive) together with its size written out in ordinary base-ten digits, most significant digit first — so the number is literally readable. Adding, subtracting, multiplying, raising to a power, comparing, dividing with a remainder, and finding the greatest common divisor are all provided, each done the way it is done by hand, and each documented in the file.

A fraction is stored as a top and a bottom, both exact whole numbers from Step 1, always reduced to lowest terms with the sign kept on the top and the bottom always positive. Adding, subtracting, multiplying, dividing, and comparing fractions are provided, each reducing the result, and each documented. A fraction can also be shown as a decimal with a chosen number of places — but only for reading; that decimal never re-enters a calculation.

- **The domain, enforced.** Every value lives strictly between zero and the One: greater than zero, and at most one. There is no zero, no negative value, and nothing exceeds the One — and because every value is an exact fraction of whole numbers, no irrational and no imaginary value can ever arise (there is no floating point or complex number anywhere in the engine). This is checked on every value as it is made: a value that breaks the domain **halts the engine** rather than being carried (`require_in_domain`). It is the theory's No-Zero Axiom, enforced. - **The One.** The single assumption: the value one. It is the only thing taken as given, and it derives from itself. - **Casting out the whole Ones.** When a calculation would push past the One, the whole Ones are removed and only the part within the One is kept; a result of a full turn returns to the One itself. - **The first move, fold.** Double a value and cast out the whole Ones. Repeating this is the engine that makes every rhythm and count in the theory. - **The second move, take.** The difference of a larger value and a smaller one — the *only* subtraction the theory permits, and only when the larger truly is the larger. - **Rhythms and turning.** From these come the period of a value (how many folds return it to itself), turning on the circle of the One, the phase of one value seen from another, and the beat between two rhythms. Every value carries, as readable text, the exact record of how it was made — for example `take(ONE, fold(supposed(1/4)))`. Because a value can only be made by these moves, every value's record traces back to the One.

- **The fold period of a unit fraction** (`fold_period_of_unit_fraction`): the fold doubles, so one-over-n cycles as one, two, four, … with the whole Ones cast out (the remainder against n). The number of folds to return to one is the period, counted with whole numbers — exactly the fold's own period. - **The two generators** (`structural_counts.ep`), read off the fold's period spectrum — nothing chosen. As `n` runs over the denominators whose orbit returns, the periods that appear are `1/3→2, 1/5→4, 1/7→3, 1/9→6, …`; the One itself has period one. The two smallest periods beyond the One are the two generators: - **the binary count** `b = 2` — the smallest fold period beyond the One (the fold's own doubling factor; also the electroweak / electromagnetic count). - **the colour count** `c = 3` — the next distinct fold period (the colour and generation count). `1/3` and `1/7` are merely where periods two and three first appear; the generators are the periods, read off the spectrum in order. Every other number in the theory is forced from these two and the One. - **The covering depth** (`minimal_binary_cover`): the smallest number of doublings whose reach covers a volume, found by doubling from the One until it first covers. It can stop at only one number. - **The enforcement** (`enforcement.ep`) — the engine polices the law itself and **halts** on any breach: - `forced_to_be` — a value may stand only if it equals an *independent* forced derivation of the same thing; a fitted or tampered value makes the two disagree, and the engine screams. - `forced_unique` — a value must be *uniquely* forced: the forced candidate must satisfy its condition and no alternative may also satisfy it. If more than one lands, the value was **selected among equals**, not forced — scream. - `forbid_selection` — an explicit stop for any place a value would be chosen, searched, or fitted. There is no legitimate selection in the theory. - `require_in_domain` (in the fold layer) — zero, negative, or past-the-One halts. - `forbid_target_input` (with the `Measured` type in `measured_values.ep`) — the measured value can never forge a derivation. A measured number is a distinct `Measured` type; the `Fraction`-only derivation primitives cannot consume it, so feeding a target into a forcing is a **compile error** (the engine will not build), with `forbid_target_input` halting at runtime as a backstop.
